title: The Manusmriti — the Sanskrit text
author: manu
attributionNote: The dharma text the tradition ascribes to Manu, the first of men, who is said to have received it from Brahma and to have taught it to the sages; it is a compilation of several hands, in which the older dharma of the schools was reshaped into the systematic code that later smriti literature quotes as its authority. GRETIL's e-text was input by Michio Yano and Yasuke Iriki.
description: The Manusmṛti is the law book of classical India: the creation and the ages, the sources of dharma, the sacraments and stages of life, the duties of the student, the householder, the ascetic and the king, marriage, inheritance, the law of debt and contract, the punishments of the court, the law of the castes and of the mixed castes, purification and penance, and the law of women and of the household. Its verses carry both the ritual and the legal order, and its chapters on the king's court and on the evidence of witnesses made it the foundation of the Sanskrit legal tradition.
historicalContext: Composed in the centuries around the turn of the era and commented on by Medhātithi, Kullūka, Govindarāja and others, the Manusmṛti became the text through which dharma was taught in the Sanskrit schools and the work the British administrators translated first. Every later smriti and digest refers to it, and Bühler's translation of it is one of the library's own English dharma texts.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all twelve adhyāyas and 2,688 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation; the library holds Bühler's English translation as The Laws of Manu.

editions.attributionText: The Manusmriti — the Sanskrit text. GRETIL e-text 2020-01-16, Göttingen Register of Electronic Texts in Indian Languages. Source edition: K: Manusmṛti with the commentary of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa, based on Shastri 1983, compared with Śāstrī 1982. M: Manusmṛti with the commentary of Medhātithi, based on the Calcutta Edition from 1967 and Jha 1992. J.L. Shastri (ed.): Manusmṛti with the Sanskrit commentary Manvartha-Muktāvalī of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa. Delhi 1983. Haragovinda Śāstrī and Gopāla Śāstrī Nene (eds.): Manusmṛti with the Manvartha-Muktāvalī of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa. Varanasi 1982 (The Kashi Sanskrit series 114). Manu: Manusmṛtiḥ medātithibhāṣyasamalaṅkṛtā. Calcutta 1967. Gaṅgānātha Jha (ed.): Manu-smṛti with the “Manubhāṣya” of Medhātithi. Delhi 1992 (Parimal Sanskrit Series 33). Input by Michio Yano and Yasuke Ikari.

The import cache stores the exact segments that were validated. The reader re-fetches the work from GRETIL and reports when the served count no longer matches the index.
